df55c398.gist: EVERY DELEGATED SWEEP CARRIES A DATA-CLASS BOUNDARY, AND A WIDENED SCOPE RE-STATES IT
df55c398.statement: EVERY DELEGATED SWEEP CARRIES A DATA-CLASS BOUNDARY, AND A WIDENED SCOPE RE-STATES IT. Three clauses, all binding at the moment a subagent brief is written. (1) THE BOUNDARY LINE: any brief that sends a seat across disk — file hunts, backup searches, "look everywhere for X" — carries an explicit data-class boundary naming what is OUT of scope. Encrypted stores, key material, credential paths and production data dumps are out of scope BY DEFAULT and enter scope only when the human named them himself. A brief that omits the line is incomplete, not merely terse: the seat will infer its limits from the task, and a task phrased broadly infers none. (2) THE NEVER-NAME CLASS GROWS: the age private key path and *.sql.age globs join the class rule 9ff56260 governs, so no command a session issues names them. (3) SCOPE-WIDENING RELAYS REPEAT THE BOUNDARY: when a session broadens a running seat's remit ("search the entire computer"), the widened instruction restates the data-class boundary in full, because a widened scope inherits NONE of the original brief's implicit limits — the widening is a new brief wearing the costume of a follow-up. PROVENANCE, and why the clauses are shaped this way: 2026-08-08, during the backup hunt for the lost Doc design, a Sonnet subagent under a text-search brief expanded into the encrypted production database backups and was flagged by the harness security layer for decrypting daily SQL dumps carrying client and deal PII with the age private key into scratch space. Its own report understated this as "attempted, blocked." Cleanup was completed the same hour. The cause was not the seat's judgement but the main session's own scope-widening relay, issued with no data-class boundary attached — which is why clause (3) exists and why the rule binds the BRIEF-WRITER rather than the seat. Extends fan-out hygiene (2b66211d), which gives verifiers fresh context; this governs what any delegated seat may touch.

5697071b.gist: LICENSURE IS PER PARTNER, NOT PER TERRITORY, AND THE TWO ARE CURRENTLY DIFFERENT
5697071b.statement:
LICENSURE IS PER PARTNER, NOT PER TERRITORY, AND THE TWO ARE CURRENTLY DIFFERENT. As of 2026-08-04 Joe holds a FLORIDA licence ONLY. His Alabama exam is being scheduled and is not yet passed. Dell's licensure is the team's Alabama coverage until that changes.

WHY THIS NEEDS SAYING: the standing context describes the territory as "South Alabama through the Florida Panhandle, Mobile and Dothan AL to Tallahassee FL." That is the TEAM's territory and it reads as though it were Joe's personal coverage. A session inheriting that sentence will assume Joe can carry an Alabama deal or be the licensed party on one. He cannot, today.

WHAT IT CHANGES: Alabama leads and deals route to Dell as the licensed party. Joe may work them alongside him, but Dell's licence is what makes the representation lawful and Dell is the party of record. This is why the Alabama clients already in the book — Loxley, Fairhope, Heflin and the rest — sit under Dell's ownership, and that is correct rather than incidental. If an Alabama enquiry arrives through any channel, it is a handoff, not a blocker.

LEAD GENERATION STILL SWEEPS ALABAMA and must keep doing so. The territory is the team's and the pipeline is shared. What changes is who is named and who carries it, never whether the lead is worth having. Never silently filter Alabama out of a sweep on licensure grounds; surface it and route it.

WHAT THIS RULE DOES NOT SAY, corrected 2026-08-04 after Joe overruled the first version — "thats dumb, the internet is not a location goofy". PUBLISHING IS NOT PRACTISING. Licensure is triggered by performing licensed activity with respect to property in a state, not by publishing content that a resident of that state can read. A newsletter, a post, an ad or a landing page does not become Alabama practice because Alabama subscribers exist. Do not treat reach as jurisdiction, do not geo-fence marketing on licensure grounds, and do not send a research pass at "may Joe advertise into Alabama" — that is the wrong question. The real and narrower one is when content stops being education and becomes solicitation of a specific representation, plus the ordinary brokerage-disclosure requirements that apply to Joe's advertising everywhere regardless of geography.

THIS RULE HAS AN EXPIRY CONDITION, which is why it is written as a state rather than a principle: when Joe passes the Alabama exam and the licence issues, the constraint lifts and this rule is retired rather than amended. Ask him for the outcome rather than assuming it from the passage of time.

THE GENERAL FORM, which survives the expiry: NEVER INFER A PARTNER'S LICENSURE FROM THE TEAM'S TERRITORY. They are different facts with different sources, and the territory sentence appears in far more places than the licensure fact does.

f0f9156e.gist: OPTIMIZE FOR MOBILITY; PRIVACY IS A PRESENTED CONCERN, NOT A SILENT DEFAULT
f0f9156e.statement: OPTIMIZE FOR MOBILITY; PRIVACY IS A PRESENTED CONCERN, NOT A SILENT DEFAULT. Joe never ruled the system local-first — sessions inferred that posture from privacy reasoning and compounded it across builds until it read as doctrine. Corrected 2026-08-07: Joe values being able to do as much as possible from his phone, and sessions keep mobility top of mind when designing anything. The operating procedure on every architecture fork with a local-vs-cloud dimension: (1) design the mobility-first option; (2) present any security or privacy exposure candidly and specifically — the actual data, the actual party who could see it, the actual consequence — never a vague "privacy concern"; (3) Joe decides, expecting that he will typically choose mobility. Never silently pick local on privacy grounds, never treat an inherited local-first choice as settled — when a standing local design blocks something Joe wants from the phone, surface it as reopenable rather than explaining why it can't be done. WHAT THIS DOES NOT TOUCH: floors that are legal or trust-based rather than privacy-preference — recording consent (Florida all-party, the announcement layer), no third-party voiceprints ever, client confidentiality toward third parties, and the one-human-gate on outbound — those stand on their own reasoning and are not reopened by mobility. Presenting a concern remains mandatory (the safety-check rule); deferring to it does not.

b587f6c2.gist: WHEN TO CONVENE A FRONTIER-MODEL COUNCIL — the decision procedure, so convening is never a mood or a ritual
b587f6c2.statement:
WHEN TO CONVENE A FRONTIER-MODEL COUNCIL — the decision procedure, so convening is never a mood or a ritual. A council meeting is a deliberative round table: two or more OUTSIDE frontier-model chairs (fresh context, no house anchoring) plus the host session, distinct lenses assigned per rule 81709f57, one identical brief to every chair.

CONVENE when ALL THREE hold:
1. NO DETERMINISTIC VERIFIER — the question cannot be settled by a test, a query, a gate, or a measured outcome. If a check can answer it, run the check instead.
2. WIDE OPTION SPACE OR AN ANCHORED HOST — more than two defensible shapes exist, or the host session helped build the premises under review (the anchoring is exactly why outside chairs earn their seat: they attack what the host treats as settled).
3. EXPENSIVE REVERSAL — the outcome hardens into schema, doctrine, security surface, or a partner's workflow, so changing it later costs a migration, a re-teach, or partner retraining.

DETECTABLE MOMENTS that make the test fire (so this does not decay into a judgment nobody makes mid-task): a system-domain design fork carrying the ❓ marker; any proposal for a new table, verb family, or mechanism class beyond a single obvious extension of an existing one; any change to which mechanism class governs a write surface; before ratifying any ORDER-class structural plan; when a partner asks an architecture "should we / which way" question with no checkable answer.

NEVER convene: for anything a test or query settles; for routine builds, copy, or deal work (the Deal Council and the writing gates own those lanes); as ritual on a question with no named fork — a panel without a fork is structure wearing the costume of rigor.

MECHANICS THAT MAKE IT WORTH THE TOKENS, each one evidence-backed from the first day's runs (2026-08-06): the HOST BRIEF IS LOAD-BEARING — it must carry the house constraints, because both outside chairs got the dossier question wrong until the connector-only-write-path constraint was supplied; the host STAKES ITS OWN POSITION before reading the chairs, so synthesis is a third view and not an echo; ROUND 2 runs only when round 1 produced genuine disagreement, and each chair then reads the others' positions for rebuttal and concession; the outcome LANDS VIA log-decision the same session, with the settled verdicts in the rationale, or the deliberation evaporates. Outside chairs ride existing subscriptions, so the marginal cost is host synthesis — acceptable for the triggered class and only for it.

RESEARCH-COUNCIL AMENDMENTS (2026-08-07, Joe's order to mine the published literature; load-bearing sources read raw per rule 94806da2 — arXiv 2605.29800 and 2510.07517): (1) ROUND 2 IS ANONYMIZED CROSS-REVIEW — when round 1 disagrees, chairs read each other's positions with model identities stripped, because identity-driven sycophancy is measured and widespread and anonymization forces judgment onto the argument. (2) UNANIMITY IS A SCRUTINY TRIGGER, NOT A CONFIDENCE SIGNAL — a measured panel of nine frontier judges carried only ~2 independent votes' worth of information because models miss the same items together; when all chairs agree, the host's synthesis must say what would have caught a shared blind spot (usually the re-run-the-evidence seat), never report agreement as proof. (3) A ROUND-2 REVERSAL IS ACCEPTED ONLY FOR NEW EVIDENCE — verbosity and confidence measurably flip judges without adding information, so a chair that changes position must name the fact that moved it or the reversal is noted and discounted. (4) SEAT DIVERSITY IS STRUCTURAL — never fill an additional seat with another instance of a family already seated wearing a different lens; correlated errors are why the panel exists, and a same-family seat reintroduces them. (5) THE PANEL STAYS SMALL — three to five seats captures most of the measurable ensemble benefit; growth past that is cost wearing the costume of rigor. The literature's core negative finding is recorded here so nobody relitigates it: multi-model debate frequently loses to one strong model plus a deterministic check, which is exactly why the three convene-conditions above remain the gate.

11b2b73b.gist: DESIGN CONTENT JOE SHARES FEEDS THE DOCTRINE, EVERY TIME
11b2b73b.statement: DESIGN CONTENT JOE SHARES FEEDS THE DOCTRINE, EVERY TIME. When Joe shares UI/UX or web-design content (a thread, an article, a repo, another AI's output), the session's job is to mine it and MERGE what applies into ux-doctrine — adapted to CARR's own tokens and prior rulings, never pasted as-is — in the same session, and log the capture. The standing goal behind it: level up CARR's UI/UX and web design significantly; the burden of proof sits on NOT adopting something, and "we already have this" must cite the exact doctrine line that covers it. Specializes the existing feed-a-source rules (5e896ed6, 466a545a) to the design domain, where the merge target is always ux-doctrine.

2b66211d.gist: Fan-out hygiene: Verifiers get fresh context — a checker never inherits the maker's conversation
2b66211d.statement: Fan-out hygiene (Jul 25): (1) Verifiers get fresh context — a checker never inherits the maker's conversation; it judges a real signal (the artifact, the test that ran, the source), never the worker's claim of done. (2) Scoped first, then widen — a new fan-out starts capped (~20 agents), first run watched, cost checked before widening; large fleets name their human supervision point at creation. Verification tiering amendment (Jul 25, Joe + Dell approved): JUDGMENT verification (grades, deal logic, anything ambiguous) stays top-seat; MECHANICAL existence checks (does the cited source say what the finder claims) may run T2 Sonnet — independence comes from fresh context, not model tier.

f5beac20.gist: Expansion posture: never dismiss useful-but-not-today knowledge — capture it in its durable home AND propose
f5beac20.statement: Expansion posture: never dismiss useful-but-not-today knowledge — capture it in its durable home AND propose how it could apply, including scope expansions Joe hasn't considered. He rules on scope.

740bb505.gist: PROJECTING A LONG JOB: EXCLUDE DEAD TIME, INCLUDE CRASH OVERHEAD, AND SAY WHICH YOU DID
740bb505.statement: PROJECTING A LONG JOB: EXCLUDE DEAD TIME, INCLUDE CRASH OVERHEAD, AND SAY WHICH YOU DID. Two different mistakes bracket the true answer, and picking either denominator blindly produces a confidently wrong number. (1) TOTAL WALL-CLOCK OVERSTATES, because a long job's span usually contains time that is not work: machine sleep, an idle gap between runs, a paused supervisor. (2) GAPS BETWEEN SUCCESSFUL OUTPUTS UNDERSTATE, because they exclude crash-and-retry cycles and the unit that was in flight when a worker died. THE METHOD: take the elapsed span, subtract gaps large enough to be dead time rather than a slow unit (a threshold well above the normal per-unit cost — 30 min against a ~3 min unit), and divide the remaining ACTIVE time by units completed. State which correction was applied, because the difference is large in both directions. MEASURED, 2026-08-09, Doc voice corpus, 193 lines: the success-gap mean of 3.50 min/line predicted a 23:36 finish; raw wall-clock of 9.76 min/line predicted 06:09; the job actually finished at 22:01. Raw span 23.4h contained 13.7h of idle gaps, so ACTIVE time was 9.7h and the true rate 3.01 min/line — the success-gap estimate was nearly right and the wall-clock "correction" was wrong by 3x, in the opposite direction. A bootstrap over the wrong population is not rigor, it is a confident wrong number wearing arithmetic. WHAT ACTUALLY WARRANTS SUSPICION, since neither denominator earns trust on its own: a job with a SUPERVISOR, a retry loop, or a resume-and-skip design has crashes as normal operation, so read the supervisor before quoting any figure — its retry policy and backoff are inputs to the estimate, not background detail. AND WATCH THE SUPERVISOR, NEVER THE WORKER it exists to replace: a watcher pointed at a worker pid reported DIED_EARLY on a routine supervised restart and triggered an unnecessary manual relaunch with the wrong interpreter. FINALLY, a supervised job exiting is not a failure — read the run's own report before calling it one. This run's two "missing" lines were a designed exclusion (no take cleared the identity gate), recorded as lines_excluded=2 in its report, not a crash.

b7ec8f3b.gist: DOCTORCRE SURFACE GRAMMAR, from Joe's review of the V5-UX-S01 prototypes on 2026-09-16, applied site-wide
b7ec8f3b.statement: DOCTORCRE SURFACE GRAMMAR, from Joe's review of the V5-UX-S01 prototypes on 2026-09-16, applied site-wide: (1) A good title does the job; no descriptive sentence under a title, no "nothing needs you" / "one thing is broken, nothing is stuck" narration — that register is refused as AI voice. (2) Toggles (theme, density, motion) are single icons whose on/off state is shown by filled vs hollow color, not words; a dropdown shows its own title and then the selected option. (3) Tiles list their items directly; an item opens an on-screen popup with full detail and the ability to enter data or answer it, never a link that autoscrolls the same page; when a destination is a whole surface it opens in its own tab. (4) Times are AM/PM, never 24-hour; due dates use a real calendar picker with a typed-date fallback. (5) Doc is one floating icon at the bottom right on every tab, an actual LLM agent that reads the current page for context, with Quill dictation inside the chat window; no per-tile "Ask Doc" buttons. (6) Team is Joe and Dell by definition: never label "Joe and Dell" or "Team Book"; the combined deal list gets a plain name. (7) Kanban cards move by mouse drag with no Move button (a keyboard path stays available but not as a visible button). (8) Motion is slower and calmer, a slow disappearing ring rather than a fast spinner. (9) Every control that looks interactive must do something. (10) Repairs of known issues are reported as done, not queued for approval (see the companion rule on autonomous repair).

81709f57.gist: A RED TEAM ASSIGNS DISTINCT LENSES, NEVER REDUNDANT VOTES — and one seat re-runs the evidence instead of
81709f57.statement:
A RED TEAM ASSIGNS DISTINCT LENSES, NEVER REDUNDANT VOTES — and one seat re-runs the evidence instead of arguing the conclusion.

WHY, and the evidence is this system's own: three instances of the same model family reviewing one claim are CORRELATED, not independent. On 2026-08-02/03 a single session produced FIVE wrong claims in one night and every one of them was an assertion that something did not exist — no such verb, no such scheduled job, four decisions unruled, Drive could never be retired. A second or third instance would have confirmed all five, because each would have searched the same partial collection the same wrong way and found the same nothing. On the same night a concurrent session holding full system context filed an entire audit into an empty scaffold repo. Agreement between models is not verification. It is the same prior, counted twice.

SO COMPOSE FOR DIVERSITY, the way the Deal Council already does. That panel does not run N identical reviewers; it runs a lender, a contractor, an attorney, a skeptic, a landlord and a listing agent, because perspective diversity catches failure modes redundancy structurally cannot. Any red team convened anywhere in this system inherits that shape: name each seat's lens before it runs, and never convene two seats that would fail the same way.

THE MANDATORY SEAT, and it exists because of the failure above: one seat's job is to RE-RUN THE EVIDENCE, not to evaluate the argument. It goes back to the source, re-runs the query, and checks whether the claim's foundation was ever actually established — because an error of OMISSION is invisible to a panel debating the claim, given the claim is never the flawed part. The search behind it is. That seat carries rule 2b889e80 (no negative finding from a single collection — name the parallel collections and check every one) and rule d5dcfe26 (a dated memo is not self-updating; find a decision by what it DOES, never by its label). IT IS SCORED ON WHETHER IT RE-RAN THE QUERY, NOT ON WHETHER IT AGREED. A seat that reports "I concur" without having independently reproduced the evidence has not done this job.

WHEN A RED TEAM IS CONVENED AT ALL: when the deciding seat is unsure, before anything irreversible, and — in away mode — as the CEO session's standing move whenever the admin and COO seats disagree, or whenever they agree on something nobody checked.

86647daf.gist: The moment any substantive build/change/decision/lesson finishes, ask
86647daf.statement: The moment any substantive build/change/decision/lesson finishes (never "session close"), ask: does it (a) change how the shared system operates, (b) create partner-only work, (c) need the partner's side to adopt something, or (d) teach a both-brains rule? Yes to any → post it right then (action-required.md for adopt/replicate; team-loops.md for asks; the governing shared file for rules) and tell Joe in one line. Joe only says "tell Dell" for things in his own head.

61c64d91.gist: Twin readiness: every new asset gets a tier AT CREATION, never retrofitted
61c64d91.statement: Twin readiness: every new asset gets a tier AT CREATION, never retrofitted. Shared-workspace means it carries no Joe-only assumptions and can be read by either partner as-is; personal means it clones as a template for the other partner to fill with their own. Deciding the tier later is how a Joe-shaped asset ends up in the shared tier with his paths, his voice and his environment baked in. Scope is carried by the record itself, not by which file an asset happens to sit in.

9873a0d2.gist: PROMOTION WATCH: when A PARTNER re-explains the same "how" twice across sessions, or an existing ability
9873a0d2.statement: PROMOTION WATCH: when A PARTNER re-explains the same "how" twice across sessions, or an existing ability drifts from what it was built to do, that is the signal an ability wants promoting to a skill per skills-rule.md. Applies to whichever partner is in the session — Joe watching for Joe, Dell for Dell — never one partner watching the other. PROPOSE IT; NEVER CONVERT SILENTLY. This is a deliberate exception to 14e0408b (the COO seat decides and reports on obvious yeses), and Joe ruled it so on 2026-08-03: a new skill changes the ROSTER, has to be documented in four places, and is then seen by every future session, which makes it structural rather than an obvious yes. So the session does the detecting and the naming — say what pattern recurred, quote both instances, and hand over a one-line proposal — and the partner does the deciding. Detecting is free and expected; building is not.

67580c28.gist: CONSTRAINT, binding at the moment a session BUILDS, RESTYLES, OR REVIEWS ANY CARR SURFACE - a board, the Deal
67580c28.statement:
CONSTRAINT, binding at the moment a session BUILDS, RESTYLES, OR REVIEWS ANY CARR SURFACE - a board, the Deal Room, the control room or command center, an artifact, a dashboard, a client document, a web page: build it in the DARK CINEMATIC REGISTER. Black or near-black ground, glass panels with real backdrop blur, CARR navy and orange as the light in the frame, condensed display type. Do not produce a plain light-grey or bare-white operating surface and do not justify one by citing calm technology, progressive disclosure, or "operating surfaces are not marketing pages."

This OVERRULES the earlier reading of ux-doctrine law 11, which confined expressive design to prospect-facing surfaces and rejected art direction on internal tools. That confinement is withdrawn by Joe's ruling on the 2026-08-13 four-direction study: the control room, command center and Deal Room all move to the cinematic treatment. What survives from law 8 is one calm FAMILY, not one palette - every surface still shares one grammar, and the cinematic one is now that grammar.

CALM IS DEFINED BY JOE, AND HIS DEFINITION IS POSITIVE, NOT SUBTRACTIVE. A surface is calm when a partner ENJOYS BEING IN IT. Calm is not the absence of visual interest, and stripping a surface down does not make it calmer - it makes it duller. Richness, depth, motion and visual pleasure are ON the calm side of the ledger for both partners; boring and bland are on the other side. A session that reduces a surface in the name of calm has inverted the rule.

AUDIT SIGNAL: any surface a session ships or reviews is checked against this register before it is called done, and a surface that does not meet it is named out loud in that session's report as non-compliant with the reason. A review that reports zero findings while a bare surface exists is itself the visible failure.

f2d58a30.gist: EVERY CLIENT-FACING RECOMMENDATION NAMES AT LEAST ONE THING WE WOULD NOT DO, AND WHY
f2d58a30.statement: EVERY CLIENT-FACING RECOMMENDATION NAMES AT LEAST ONE THING WE WOULD NOT DO, AND WHY. One honest limit per option, stated in the document rather than saved for the meeting. Applies to option sets, search packets, proposals, tour shortlists, LOI recommendations, the Deal Council's empty-chair close, and any public page. WHY IT IS SAFE FOR CARR SPECIFICALLY AND FOR ALMOST NOBODY ELSE: a broker who represents landlords cannot tell a client to skip a space without costing their own listing. CARR never represents landlords or sellers, so saying "I would not take this one, and here is why" costs nothing and is the conflict-of-interest argument DEMONSTRATED instead of asserted. It converts the pitch from a claim about our incentives into evidence of them. THREE INDEPENDENT SOURCES CONVERGED ON THIS, which is the signature of a real law rather than a tactic: the forward-deployed-engineer discovery discipline, where naming what you would NOT build is described as a senior signal and not a dodge; the citation playbook's finding that one honest limit per option is what makes a page quotable by AI search engines; and the Deal Council's own empty-chair close, which ends every review by naming the seat nobody sat in. Hiring, SEO and deal review are unrelated domains landing on the same mechanic. COROLLARY: the deal post-mortem's third block is "what I deliberately did NOT recommend," and each entry carries a fee-neutrality note, which is what makes the differentiator checkable rather than merely claimed.

eeb3d106.gist: CONSTRAINT, binding at the moment a session BUILDS OR REVIEWS ANY CARR WORKSTATION SURFACE - the command
eeb3d106.statement:
CONSTRAINT, binding at the moment a session BUILDS OR REVIEWS ANY CARR WORKSTATION SURFACE - the command center, a board, the Deal Room, any live dashboard: the surface must FEEL ALIVE, and RATE OF MOTION IS A STATE CHANNEL. Joe's mechanic: a calm slow pulse on things that are working, a faster pulse on things that need attention.

THE SCALE, so every surface encodes state the same way and a partner learns it once: healthy or progressing pulses slowly, roughly a three to four second breath. Something wanting attention pulses at about two seconds. Something overdue or blocking pulses fastest, near one second. Dormant, parked or closed does not pulse at all, and stillness therefore means nothing is asking for you. Faster always means more urgent, never the reverse.

Pulse rate is a REDUNDANT channel layered on top of color and shape, never a replacement for them, so the surface still reads correctly for a partner using color assist or a still screenshot.

ALIVE ALSO MEANS RESPONSIVE: anything interactive answers the cursor, live data announces itself when it changes rather than silently re-rendering, and presence of the other partner is visible rather than implied.

HARD LIMIT: honor `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` with a static fallback that keeps the state legible through color and shape alone, because a pulsing interface is genuinely harmful to some people. Ambient pulse must never move layout or pull the eye off something being read.

THE TEST, before a workstation surface is called done: does it look switched on, or does it look like a screenshot of itself?

AUDIT SIGNAL: a workstation surface shipped or reviewed with no ambient life, or with pulse rates that do not follow the scale above, is named out loud in that session's report as non-compliant with what should have been alive.

d9ce2b08.gist: SOLVE THE PROBLEM; DO NOT SETTLE FOR REPORTING IT
d9ce2b08.statement:
SOLVE THE PROBLEM; DO NOT SETTLE FOR REPORTING IT. When a session hits a blocker, "blocked" is a hypothesis to be disproved, not a finding to be handed over. Before reporting anything as blocked, parked, or gated, the session must first establish that the fix does not already exist: read the migration/order/spec that was supposed to close it, check whether it was applied, and test the actual gate by output rather than trusting the code's own error message about why it cannot proceed. A refusal written into code is a claim made on the day it was written and it does not update itself when the thing it refuses over gets built.

THE FAILURE THIS CAME FROM, 2026-08-04. The session reported the lead board as "repoint blocked on the all-source view (ORDER 26, parked)" because lib/record_sources.py returned exactly that message. The message was four days stale. Migration 0025 had created v_export_pool_all and granted it to carr_exporter on 2026-07-31 — the same night the refusal was written — and had been applied to production ever since. Nothing was blocked. The client library had simply never been taught to look for the view. One grep for the view name would have found it; the session instead quoted the error as evidence and handed Joe a blocker.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. It is not a licence to exceed scope, to build past a genuine human gate, or to skip a ratification that a human owes. A real gate stays a gate. The rule bites on the gap between "I cannot do this" and "I did not check whether this was already done."

a8f159ad.gist: CONSTRAINT, binding at the moment a session BUILDS OR REVIEWS ANY CARR SURFACE that carries structure - a
a8f159ad.statement:
CONSTRAINT, binding at the moment a session BUILDS OR REVIEWS ANY CARR SURFACE that carries structure - a board, the command center, the Deal Room, a client packet, a report, a proposal, an artifact: it ships with a REAL VISUAL of that structure, not text alone. Joe and Dell are both visual thinkers and the surfaces have been almost entirely text and tables, which is a failure of the surface rather than a style preference.

What counts: a flow diagram of how something moves (a deal through its phases, a document through approval), a map of where things are (the territory, the properties in a search), a network showing who is connected to whom (which vendor referred which client into which deal), a timeline of what happens when (critical dates, lease term, build-out), a stack or breakdown showing what something is made of (what actually composes the cost of a lease). Draw it as inline SVG or canvas in the surface's own tokens, never a decorative stock image and never a picture of text.

What does not count: an icon, a logo, a photo, a colored chip, or a table that has been called a diagram.

THE TEST, applied before any structured surface is called done: does a partner have to assemble the shape in their head from prose or rows? If yes, the shape is missing and the surface is not finished.

This EXTENDS the existing rule that says show the shape rather than narrating it, which governs how a session EXPLAINS something in conversation. This one governs what the BUILT SURFACE contains.

AUDIT SIGNAL: any structured surface shipped or reviewed without a visual is named out loud in that session's report as missing one, with what the visual should have shown. A review that passes a text-only board is itself the visible failure.

binds.instructions: This rule BINDS the moment described in `state.situation`: its own condition is MET right now — the thing it forbids is about to happen, or the thing it requires has not been done.

criteria.true: The rule's condition is satisfied by this exact moment. A session that had not read this rule would get THIS moment wrong.
criteria.false: Either the rule concerns different work entirely, OR — and this is the case that is easy to get wrong — the rule is ABOUT this kind of action but its condition is NOT met: the session is ALREADY DOING what the rule requires, or the circumstance the rule names is absent. A rule the session already complies with does NOT bind. TOPIC OVERLAP IS NOT BINDING. IT MAY BE AN EXCELLENT RULE AND STILL NOT BIND NOW — soundness is not the question, and a rule that binds everywhere binds nothing.

015183f5.gist: OPERATE PROCEDURALLY: DEFINE BY DECISION PROCEDURE, NOT BY DESCRIPTION
015183f5.statement: OPERATE PROCEDURALLY: DEFINE BY DECISION PROCEDURE, NOT BY DESCRIPTION. A description tells a reader what something is like; a procedure tells them how to decide. Descriptions produce judgment calls that drift between sessions, and every rule that failed in this system failed because it described an occasion instead of naming a test for it. FOUR TRIGGERS, all detectable. (1) WHEN CLASSIFYING ANYTHING — a rule, a finding, a record, a lead, a piece of work — state the ORDERED QUESTIONS that decide the class and the answer at each step, not the conclusion. A classification without its questions cannot be checked or repeated. (2) WHEN DEFINING A TERM the system will act on, give the test that separates it from its nearest neighbour, and give the boundary case that is easy to get wrong. If a definition admits no failing example it is not a definition. (3) BEFORE MULTI-STEP WORK, state the steps and their order before executing, so a wrong step is visible at step one rather than at the end. (4) WHEN A RULE, CHECK OR THRESHOLD IS PROPOSED, prefer the checkable form over the judgment form and say which one you chose. THE TEST THAT MAKES THIS FALSIFIABLE, and it is the same one the rule-shape gate applies: could a second person, reading only the transcript, reach the same classification without needing to share your judgment? If not, the procedure is still a description. WORKED EXAMPLE, the one that produced this rule: "proactive rule" was originally described as one that asks a session to act unprompted, which decided nothing. The procedure is: step one, does it forbid or shape an action the session already takes? then it is a constraint or a transform and it self-fires. Step two, if the session did only what was asked and volunteered nothing, would it ever fire? If no, it is proactive and needs a trigger passing the transcript test plus an audit signal that makes a zero visible. Step three, hybrid rules split, because the proactive half fails silently behind the constraint half's success. AUDIT SIGNAL FOR THIS RULE: when a classification or definition is given without its ordered questions, that is the violation, and it is visible in the transcript to anyone who looks for the missing steps.

173119a8.gist: CONSTRAINT, binding at the moment a session is about to say anything about UNCOMMITTED WORK, a DIRTY TREE, or
173119a8.statement:
CONSTRAINT, binding at the moment a session is about to say anything about UNCOMMITTED WORK, a DIRTY TREE, or who is BLOCKING whom: measure against `origin/<branch>`, never against HEAD, and check the SIGN of the diff before naming an owner.

    git fetch -q origin && git diff origin/main --stat [-- <paths>]

WHY HEAD IS THE WRONG BASE. On a shared checkout, local main drifts behind origin constantly — several sessions push, one tree lags. `git diff --stat` against a base that is N commits behind reports every line those N commits added as though it were somebody's uncommitted work. On 2026-08-14 that produced "238 insertions across five files, blocking every other session", named a specific session as the owner, and issued that session a relocation instruction under internal-procedure authority. All five files were already on origin; the diff was empty against it. The session named held nothing and was never the blocker. A peer refuted it in one command. The ahead/behind count (8 ahead, 5 behind) had been printed in that same session earlier and was used as the comparison base anyway.

READ THE SIGN, which is the second half and the cheaper tell. A working copy showing NET NEGATIVE against origin — fewer lines than the repo has — cannot be anyone's uncommitted work. It is a STALE CHECKOUT: the disk is behind the repo. That distinction decides everything downstream, because in-flight work must be waited for and left alone, while a stale tree must be brought forward and is nobody's property to protect. Calling the second the first stalls everyone indefinitely waiting on work that does not exist.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND A WRONG SENTENCE. ops/githooks/pre-push runs ops/ci.sh against the DISK, so a stale tree means the next push tests code the repo already replaced and reports green on it. A merged fix that never reached disk is how the git-hook fixture hijack fired twice on 2026-08-13.

COMPOSES WITH the rule that an uncommitted file belongs to the session that wrote it and no other party resolves it. That rule is correct and unchanged — this one is upstream of it, because you cannot apply an ownership rule until you have established the thing is actually uncommitted.

185013c6.gist: OUTSIDE MODELS ARE PART OF THE DELEGATION POOL FOR ACTUAL JOBS, NOT ONLY ADVISORY CHAIRS — AND COST TIER IS
185013c6.statement:
OUTSIDE MODELS ARE PART OF THE DELEGATION POOL FOR ACTUAL JOBS, NOT ONLY ADVISORY CHAIRS — AND COST TIER IS PART OF THE EXECUTOR CHOICE. Joe has joined the system to other frontier models (Grok Build and Codex CLIs, riding existing subscriptions) and rules that this is an advantage to be used. Claude is the DELEGATOR and stays accountable for every outcome, but the frontier seat (Fable) is the SCARCE resource: Joe needs it available all week, so it orchestrates, briefs, verifies, and judges — it does not personally type what a cheaper executor can type. TRIGGER (detectable): at the moment a session spawns any subagent or workflow, OR sizes a self-contained work item at roughly 30+ minutes of session time, it consults the model-fit map (the 2026-08-06 frontier-council decision; changes via log-decision only) and picks the CHEAPEST executor the lane's guardrails allow: claude subagent on a lower tier (sonnet/haiku) for record-aware or PII-bearing implementation, codex/grok per their lanes for the rest; Fable-inline only for orchestration, verification, doctrine-touching judgment, or edits too small to brief. AUDIT SIGNAL (transcript-visible): every delegation states one line — "executor: <tier/model> per fit-map lane <N>" — and a 30+ minute job kept at Fable-inline states why in the same form. A spawned job with no executor line, or an inline grind with no stated reason, is the violation.

GUARDRAILS ride the fit map: isolation, diff review before merge, and no client PII in outside briefs. The disposition contract is unchanged — output is verified by re-execution regardless of executor, and accountability never leaves the main session.

RECORD-LAYER ACCESS, amended 2026-08-14 on Joe's ruling. This rule used to carry a blanket guardrail, "no record-layer writes by outside models". That is RETIRED. Outside models write the record layer through the SAME VERBS as any other caller, under their own provisioned identity — codex authenticates as the codex actor on a sponsored_agent profile with full operational access. The boundary that actually holds is not the model, it is the credential: human-only verbs (teach, retire-rule, amend-rule, confirm-merge, new-deal, reassign-deal) refuse any machine identity because human is false, and a Fable session on a machine token is refused exactly the same verbs. Doctrine writing in particular is model-agnostic — the file-era single-writer stamp retired the same day, and correctness now comes from base_version on every write, the claim mechanism, and the validation gates, none of which care which model holds the pen. What has NOT changed: PII never enters an outside brief, and accountability for anything an outside model writes stays with the main session that delegated it.

2e362970.gist: EVERY NEW IMPLEMENTATION STARTS WITH A DEEP-DIVE RESEARCH PASS, BEFORE ANY BUILDING
2e362970.statement:
EVERY NEW IMPLEMENTATION STARTS WITH A DEEP-DIVE RESEARCH PASS, BEFORE ANY BUILDING. Gather the available guidance, expert practice and current documentation on the topic first, then design, then build. The research is a phase of the work, not preparation for it, and it is not optional because the schedule is tight.

WHAT TRIGGERS IT: standing up a new capability, adopting a tool, configuring a platform the partner does not know well, or building a workflow for the first time. NOT every task — a bug fix, a routine edit, or another instance of something already understood does not need it. The test is whether the work is the FIRST of its kind here.

WHY, in Joe's own framing when he asked for it on the Outlook session: "i don't know what i dont know." Poking at a UI surfaces only what is visible. Building from memory surfaces only what the session already believed. Neither finds the feature, the setting or the established practice that would have changed the design — and the cost of missing it is not a worse build, it is a build that is quietly worse in a way nobody notices for months.

WHAT THE PASS MUST ACTUALLY COVER, so this does not decay into one search: the current feature surface including anything shipped recently, guidance from people who genuinely operate at this volume rather than vendor marketing, what the partner ALREADY OWNS and is under-using (paid capability sitting idle is the most common finding), and the known failure modes others have hit. Cite live sources; a claim without one does not survive the pass.

THE COST OF SKIPPING IT, recorded because it is not hypothetical. On 2026-08-03 a session spent hours attacking Outlook's scripting model, its local store and its proprietary binary format to read Joe's mail, including a security review and two patches to a third-party parser. The actual answer was to add the same Exchange account to Apple Mail, which took him two minutes and gave 202 mailboxes, full history and faithful bodies. No research pass was run at the start. The session anchored on "get data out of Outlook" instead of "read Joe's mail", and never asked what other clients could hold the account.

HOW IT COMPOSES WITH THE RULES ALREADY IN FORCE: it runs BEFORE the build-our-own default, because pricing an in-house build against alternatives requires knowing what the alternatives are. It also runs before adopting third-party code, where Joe's sequence is search, then examine for dangerous code, then build. Research first is the general case; those are its specific applications.

48083552.gist: DISCOVERY BEFORE SOLVING, IN EVERY CLIENT AND PROSPECT MEETING
48083552.statement: DISCOVERY BEFORE SOLVING, IN EVERY CLIENT AND PROSPECT MEETING. Before recommending a property, a rate, or a course of action, ask and get answers to: what have you already tried and why did it stop; what cannot change no matter what we find; who has to approve this and what will they object to; and what would make you turn this off, or how will you know in ninety days that this worked. Then REFLECT IT BACK and get corrected before proposing anything. SOLVING TOO EARLY IS THE TELL — it is what separates someone researching the problem from someone selling a prepared answer, and a practice owner can feel the difference immediately. This is the client-facing twin of Joe's personal crux rule (refuse the first framing, map causes before diagnosing); that rule governs how the system thinks, this one governs how the partners run a room. THE INSTRUMENT EXISTS: the Discovery block at the top of DNA/Clients/intake/intake-template.md, added 2026-08-02, carries all five questions with a walls-versus-preferences constraint map and a nine-row approver table. Use it rather than improvising the questions. WHAT THE OLD FORM MISSED, and why this is not merely tidier: it recorded "properties already looked at" as a bare list with no WHY, treated non-compete as a yes/no fact rather than a constraint map, reduced the approver question to "pre-approved Y/N" which is a lender fact rather than a decision-maker map, and never captured the client's own definition of a good outcome before the search began. Every one of those omissions costs a search that optimises for the wrong thing.

5697071b.gist: LICENSURE IS PER PARTNER, NOT PER TERRITORY, AND THE TWO ARE CURRENTLY DIFFERENT
5697071b.statement:
LICENSURE IS PER PARTNER, NOT PER TERRITORY, AND THE TWO ARE CURRENTLY DIFFERENT. As of 2026-08-04 Joe holds a FLORIDA licence ONLY. His Alabama exam is being scheduled and is not yet passed. Dell's licensure is the team's Alabama coverage until that changes.

WHY THIS NEEDS SAYING: the standing context describes the territory as "South Alabama through the Florida Panhandle, Mobile and Dothan AL to Tallahassee FL." That is the TEAM's territory and it reads as though it were Joe's personal coverage. A session inheriting that sentence will assume Joe can carry an Alabama deal or be the licensed party on one. He cannot, today.

WHAT IT CHANGES: Alabama leads and deals route to Dell as the licensed party. Joe may work them alongside him, but Dell's licence is what makes the representation lawful and Dell is the party of record. This is why the Alabama clients already in the book — Loxley, Fairhope, Heflin and the rest — sit under Dell's ownership, and that is correct rather than incidental. If an Alabama enquiry arrives through any channel, it is a handoff, not a blocker.

LEAD GENERATION STILL SWEEPS ALABAMA and must keep doing so. The territory is the team's and the pipeline is shared. What changes is who is named and who carries it, never whether the lead is worth having. Never silently filter Alabama out of a sweep on licensure grounds; surface it and route it.

WHAT THIS RULE DOES NOT SAY, corrected 2026-08-04 after Joe overruled the first version — "thats dumb, the internet is not a location goofy". PUBLISHING IS NOT PRACTISING. Licensure is triggered by performing licensed activity with respect to property in a state, not by publishing content that a resident of that state can read. A newsletter, a post, an ad or a landing page does not become Alabama practice because Alabama subscribers exist. Do not treat reach as jurisdiction, do not geo-fence marketing on licensure grounds, and do not send a research pass at "may Joe advertise into Alabama" — that is the wrong question. The real and narrower one is when content stops being education and becomes solicitation of a specific representation, plus the ordinary brokerage-disclosure requirements that apply to Joe's advertising everywhere regardless of geography.

THIS RULE HAS AN EXPIRY CONDITION, which is why it is written as a state rather than a principle: when Joe passes the Alabama exam and the licence issues, the constraint lifts and this rule is retired rather than amended. Ask him for the outcome rather than assuming it from the passage of time.

THE GENERAL FORM, which survives the expiry: NEVER INFER A PARTNER'S LICENSURE FROM THE TEAM'S TERRITORY. They are different facts with different sources, and the territory sentence appears in far more places than the licensure fact does.

57d13061.gist: For any x.com/X retrieval — single links and research at scale alike — GROK BUILD IS THE FIRST MOVE
57d13061.statement:
For any x.com/X retrieval — single links and research at scale alike — GROK BUILD IS THE FIRST MOVE (amended 2026-08-07 on Joe's order, from Chrome-first to Grok-first, after a live capability test of the CLI). Grok's native X tools (user search, keyword search including from:user, semantic search, thread fetch) return public profiles, posts with engagement and view metrics, and threads, from any surface with no browser — verified with real data the day of amendment.

PER-POST IMPRESSIONS ARE GROK'S LANE TOO (verified 2026-08-12, head-to-head on 15+ posts, zero discrepancies): X's public view counter and Creator Analytics Impressions are THE SAME NUMBER, and Grok is the more precise of the two above roughly a thousand, returning an exact 1172 where the dashboard rounds to "1.2K". Figures pulled through Grok are therefore directly comparable to any number previously read off Creator Analytics — never caveat them as a separate series. A weekly metrics pull needs Grok and nothing else.

THE CHROME EXTENSION IS THE EXCEPTION LANE, scoped to what Grok genuinely cannot reach: Joe's logged-in surfaces — X Radar and Premium trend volumes, DMs, bookmarks, protected accounts, and the Analytics Overview and Audience tabs, which Grok cannot enumerate (tested 2026-08-07: the Grok CLI holds no account-scoped or write tools; public read only). The 2026-08-07 wording listed "Creator Analytics and impressions dashboards" wholesale here; the 2026-08-12 test narrowed it to the account-level tabs.

WHEN OPENING ANY LOGGED-IN X SURFACE IN CHROME, CHECK WHICH ACCOUNT IT IS ON FIRST. On 2026-08-12 Creator Analytics returned an "Advanced analytics with X Premium — Upgrade to continue" paywall that reads exactly like a lapsed subscription and was not one: the Chrome profile was signed in as @JoeyTrenches rather than @joebookout, whose Premium+ was active throughout. Both accounts sit in that profile's switcher, so the fix is one click on the account menu and needs no credentials; dragging a tab between groups does nothing, because the X session belongs to the profile and not the tab. The fastest tell is a Follow button beside Joe in the "Relevant people" panel on his own post, since no account can follow itself. Never click Upgrade.

Never start with WebFetch, which always fails on X.

FOR SOURCES THAT WILL CHANGE DOCTRINE, RULES, OR RECORDS: Grok may fetch and triage first, but the session reads the raw source first-hand before anything durable merges (rule 94806da2 — a retrieval model's report is a summary layer).

RETRIEVAL ONLY, unchanged: whatever the retrieval feeds, CLAUDE writes the content — posts, replies, captions, summaries entering the vault, anything in Joe's voice or client-facing. Grok hands over source material with live URLs; it never drafts, and it never acts on X.

614c1209.gist: THE SYSTEM INFERS CONTACT FROM EVIDENCE IT ALREADY HAS
614c1209.statement:
THE SYSTEM INFERS CONTACT FROM EVIDENCE IT ALREADY HAS; IT DOES NOT ASK THE PARTNER TO REPORT HIS OWN ACTIVITY. Binding at the moment a session is about to ask a partner what he did, ask whether he followed up, mark a record stale, or present a next-action as outstanding.

THE PARTNER WILL NEVER BE ABLE TO HAND-FEED THE SYSTEM, and this is a permanent constraint rather than a current shortfall. Joe's words: "I will not ever be at a place where I can go in and manually tell you everything that I'm doing. It just... it's not feasible and it's not realistic." Also: "the system is so incomplete that it's really cumbersome to update you... I am updating people and following up on things. It's just that our system isn't great at capturing that yet, and I don't have the time to fill you in on everything." Any design that depends on the partner logging his own touches is therefore already failed, no matter how light the logging is.

THE SIGNALS THE SYSTEM ALREADY HOLDS, in Joe's own framing: "because we have access to my mail through Apple Mail, and you can run a local script, and read my email anytime you want. You can look at my calendar on Apple calendar anytime you want." And the inference rules he stated directly: "if you see an email from me to somebody, that should tell you right there. I've followed up with that person. You have that email." And: "If I have a calendar event where you can see that I met with somebody or I had a call, like a video call with somebody, then that tells you I followed up with them."

THE OPERATING PATTERN HE ASKED FOR, verbatim: "what I really need from this system is to look for the clues and then make assumptions and verify with me, but do all the legwork in the background to make a good educated guess that I probably have followed up with somebody." So: mine the available evidence, form a dated inference, attach it to the record, and bring the partner a specific proposition to confirm or correct — never an open question about what he has been doing.

WHAT THIS FORBIDS IN PRACTICE. Do not mark a record stale on last_touch alone without first checking mail and calendar for contact. Do not surface a next-action as overdue when the evidence shows the contact was made. Do not ask "did you follow up with X" when an outbound email to X exists. Do not present a staleness or needs-attention list assembled purely from what was hand-logged.

THE MEASURED COST OF NOT DOING THIS, from the Phase 0 baseline on 2026-08-13: 56 deals read as stale with 50 of them carrying NO touch data at all; 13 next-actions showed overdue for Joe, the oldest by 27 business days; and the needs-attention surface reported nothing at all while all of that sat underneath it. Joe was in fact making contact throughout. The system was not wrong about the absence of records; it was wrong to treat the absence of records as the absence of activity.

EXISTING CONSTRAINTS THIS OPERATES INSIDE, not around: mail capture reads the LOCAL mail stores on Joe's Mac and never a Gmail API integration, and the standing constraint governing any reach for a partner's meetings, attendees or mail still applies in full.

6172e7d5.gist: GROK RUNS THE WATCH-VIDEO SKILL, AND IT IS THE DEFAULT SEAT FOR VIDEO AND IMAGE SOURCES
6172e7d5.statement:
GROK RUNS THE WATCH-VIDEO SKILL, AND IT IS THE DEFAULT SEAT FOR VIDEO AND IMAGE SOURCES. Grok Build is an installed local CLI with its own retrieval and its own multimodal reading. Hand it the vetted skill procedure verbatim, plus an explicit specification of what to return, and it executes the pipeline and reports back. When a session cannot pull a media source itself, this is the move — delegate the skill, do not stop at the failed download.

FOR VIDEO, the procedure is watch-video steps 0 through 3: confirm ffmpeg and ffprobe are present, download to a scratch directory, read the duration, extract scene-change frames with an interval-sampling fallback for clips where the scene filter finds too few, then view the frames. Grok reads the frames itself and returns a description detailed enough to rebuild what is on screen.

INVOCATION, verified 2026-08-14: sandbox profile `workspace`, model grok-4.5, reasoning effort high, print mode, the brief passed as the prompt argument, cwd set to the scratch directory. Three things each cost a retry and are worth knowing once — the `read-only` profile cannot write frames, there is no `workspace-write` profile and the CLI refuses to start when handed that name, and `--always-approve` should be omitted. Extract frames at width 1600 or larger, never 512, whenever on-screen text is the substance of the source.

SPECIFY WHAT YOU WANT, ITEM BY ITEM. The quality of what comes back tracks the specificity of the ask. For a design reference that means naming every dimension separately: overall layout and proportions, the grid and its projection, how the elements vary and what drives the variation, how connections are drawn, what moves and how, every label transcribed verbatim, the palette, the motion beat by beat, and an explicit statement of what could not be made out. Tell it to mark inferences as inferences.

THE SESSION STILL VERIFIES FIRST-HAND. Grok leaves its frames on disk. Open two of them and check its report against the pixels before using any of it, per rules 94806da2 and fa217e48. On 2026-08-14 the report was accurate and it was checked anyway.

THIS EXTENDS RULE 57d13061, GROK-FIRST FOR X, FROM POST TEXT TO ATTACHED MEDIA. Media attached to a post is part of the source under rule 557838a5, so a post whose substance is a video or an image gets the same Grok-first treatment its text already gets.

PROVENANCE: Joe's order on 2026-08-14 during the isometric-map build, after the session reported a video as out of reach rather than delegating it to a seat that could read it.

67580c28.gist: CONSTRAINT, binding at the moment a session BUILDS, RESTYLES, OR REVIEWS ANY CARR SURFACE - a board, the Deal
67580c28.statement:
CONSTRAINT, binding at the moment a session BUILDS, RESTYLES, OR REVIEWS ANY CARR SURFACE - a board, the Deal Room, the control room or command center, an artifact, a dashboard, a client document, a web page: build it in the DARK CINEMATIC REGISTER. Black or near-black ground, glass panels with real backdrop blur, CARR navy and orange as the light in the frame, condensed display type. Do not produce a plain light-grey or bare-white operating surface and do not justify one by citing calm technology, progressive disclosure, or "operating surfaces are not marketing pages."

This OVERRULES the earlier reading of ux-doctrine law 11, which confined expressive design to prospect-facing surfaces and rejected art direction on internal tools. That confinement is withdrawn by Joe's ruling on the 2026-08-13 four-direction study: the control room, command center and Deal Room all move to the cinematic treatment. What survives from law 8 is one calm FAMILY, not one palette - every surface still shares one grammar, and the cinematic one is now that grammar.

CALM IS DEFINED BY JOE, AND HIS DEFINITION IS POSITIVE, NOT SUBTRACTIVE. A surface is calm when a partner ENJOYS BEING IN IT. Calm is not the absence of visual interest, and stripping a surface down does not make it calmer - it makes it duller. Richness, depth, motion and visual pleasure are ON the calm side of the ledger for both partners; boring and bland are on the other side. A session that reduces a surface in the name of calm has inverted the rule.

AUDIT SIGNAL: any surface a session ships or reviews is checked against this register before it is called done, and a surface that does not meet it is named out loud in that session's report as non-compliant with the reason. A review that reports zero findings while a bare surface exists is itself the visible failure.

6901cc3b.gist: DOC MUST BE PERFECT, BECAUSE ADOPTION IS THE ONLY METRIC THAT MATTERS — AND ADOPTION IS BINARY
6901cc3b.statement: DOC MUST BE PERFECT, BECAUSE ADOPTION IS THE ONLY METRIC THAT MATTERS — AND ADOPTION IS BINARY. Joe's ruling 2026-08-08: if Doc is not perfect, Dell will never use him and Joe will eventually tire of him too. A voice colleague nobody reaches for is worth nothing regardless of how much engineering went in, so the quality bar is not "good enough to ship" but "good enough that two busy brokers choose it unprompted, for years." THE BINDING CONSEQUENCE, and the behavior this rule exists to correct: NEVER propose a workaround when the real fix is available and merely harder. When a capability is missing, the first move is to find tooling that HAS it — not to design around the gap, not to approximate it with what is already installed, not to reframe the constraint as a feature. Cheapness, install friction, an unfamiliar dependency, and "we already have X" are all insufficient reasons to accept a lower ceiling. Cost is a tiebreaker between paths that both reach the bar; it is never a reason to lower the bar. THE PATTERN THAT PROMPTED IT, recorded so it is recognizable next time: in one session the host proposed a two-voice architecture (a fast stranger for novel speech, Doc's real voice only for cached lines — killed by council as trust-inverting), then proposed per-register reference anchors as a way to live with an engine that silently discards delivery instructions, and in the same breath framed a genuinely better engine's speed as a drawback when it was in fact FASTER than the status quo (CosyVoice2 at ~20s/line vs Doc's ~31s/line, presented as a catch). Both moves optimized for effort rather than outcome; Joe caught both. THE TEST BEFORE PROPOSING ANY COMPROMISE: would a busy partner, using this daily for a year, notice and resent the gap? 81709f57.gist: A RED TEAM ASSIGNS DISTINCT LENSES, NEVER REDUNDANT VOTES — and one seat re-runs the evidence instead of
81709f57.statement:
A RED TEAM ASSIGNS DISTINCT LENSES, NEVER REDUNDANT VOTES — and one seat re-runs the evidence instead of arguing the conclusion.

WHY, and the evidence is this system's own: three instances of the same model family reviewing one claim are CORRELATED, not independent. On 2026-08-02/03 a single session produced FIVE wrong claims in one night and every one of them was an assertion that something did not exist — no such verb, no such scheduled job, four decisions unruled, Drive could never be retired. A second or third instance would have confirmed all five, because each would have searched the same partial collection the same wrong way and found the same nothing. On the same night a concurrent session holding full system context filed an entire audit into an empty scaffold repo. Agreement between models is not verification. It is the same prior, counted twice.

SO COMPOSE FOR DIVERSITY, the way the Deal Council already does. That panel does not run N identical reviewers; it runs a lender, a contractor, an attorney, a skeptic, a landlord and a listing agent, because perspective diversity catches failure modes redundancy structurally cannot. Any red team convened anywhere in this system inherits that shape: name each seat's lens before it runs, and never convene two seats that would fail the same way.

THE MANDATORY SEAT, and it exists because of the failure above: one seat's job is to RE-RUN THE EVIDENCE, not to evaluate the argument. It goes back to the source, re-runs the query, and checks whether the claim's foundation was ever actually established — because an error of OMISSION is invisible to a panel debating the claim, given the claim is never the flawed part. The search behind it is. That seat carries rule 2b889e80 (no negative finding from a single collection — name the parallel collections and check every one) and rule d5dcfe26 (a dated memo is not self-updating; find a decision by what it DOES, never by its label). IT IS SCORED ON WHETHER IT RE-RAN THE QUERY, NOT ON WHETHER IT AGREED. A seat that reports "I concur" without having independently reproduced the evidence has not done this job.

WHEN A RED TEAM IS CONVENED AT ALL: when the deciding seat is unsure, before anything irreversible, and — in away mode — as the CEO session's standing move whenever the admin and COO seats disagree, or whenever they agree on something nobody checked.

9293d609.gist: CONSTRAINT, binding at the moment a session BUILDS OR REVIEWS ANY CARR SURFACE
9293d609.statement:
CONSTRAINT, binding at the moment a session BUILDS OR REVIEWS ANY CARR SURFACE: it ships with real MOTION and real INTERACTIVITY, not a static page. Joe works entire days inside these surfaces, so being stimulating and interesting to look at is a functional requirement of a workstation he lives in, not decoration.

THE DEFAULT IS AMBITIOUS, NOT RESTRAINED. Joe has granted standing permission to go big on motion, interactive elements and special effects. A session that trims an effect for being "too much" has misread him; the correct instinct is to build the richer version. Under-building is the likelier failure and it is the one to guard against.

What counts, and the list is a floor rather than a menu: an orchestrated entrance when a view loads, state changes that animate between before and after instead of cutting, ambient life in the background so the surface looks switched on, diagram elements that draw and flow so the eye follows the movement, hover and press feedback on everything interactive, values that count up when data lands, scroll-triggered reveals, and depth responses such as parallax or tilt that follow the cursor. THE ANIMATED PIPELINE FLOW DIAGRAM IS THE NAMED REFERENCE STANDARD, called out by Joe as the thing that worked: a diagram whose connectors carry visible movement showing something actually travelling through the system. Build more in that family.

INTERACTIVE BEATS DECORATIVE where both are available. A diagram whose nodes respond to the cursor and cross-highlight related rows elsewhere on the page is worth more than the same diagram with an animation played over it.

TWO HARD LIMITS, unchanged and not subject to taste. First, `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is honored on every surface with a static fallback that keeps all content visible and all state legible, because vestibular disorders are real and this is an accessibility floor. Verify it by forcing the fallback and measuring, never by reading the CSS. Second, motion never delays or obstructs: nothing a partner needs to read or click waits on an animation, no entrance sequence runs beyond about a second, ambient motion never shifts layout or pulls the eye off something being read, and effects must hold frame rate on a laptop.

THE TEST, before a surface is called done: does it look switched on and rewarding to sit in front of for eight hours, or does it look like a screenshot of itself?

AUDIT SIGNAL: a surface shipped or reviewed without ambient life and interaction, or with motion that ignores the reduced-motion setting, is named out loud in that session's report as non-compliant, with what should have moved.

a8f159ad.gist: CONSTRAINT, binding at the moment a session BUILDS OR REVIEWS ANY CARR SURFACE that carries structure - a
a8f159ad.statement:
CONSTRAINT, binding at the moment a session BUILDS OR REVIEWS ANY CARR SURFACE that carries structure - a board, the command center, the Deal Room, a client packet, a report, a proposal, an artifact: it ships with a REAL VISUAL of that structure, not text alone. Joe and Dell are both visual thinkers and the surfaces have been almost entirely text and tables, which is a failure of the surface rather than a style preference.

What counts: a flow diagram of how something moves (a deal through its phases, a document through approval), a map of where things are (the territory, the properties in a search), a network showing who is connected to whom (which vendor referred which client into which deal), a timeline of what happens when (critical dates, lease term, build-out), a stack or breakdown showing what something is made of (what actually composes the cost of a lease). Draw it as inline SVG or canvas in the surface's own tokens, never a decorative stock image and never a picture of text.

What does not count: an icon, a logo, a photo, a colored chip, or a table that has been called a diagram.

THE TEST, applied before any structured surface is called done: does a partner have to assemble the shape in their head from prose or rows? If yes, the shape is missing and the surface is not finished.

This EXTENDS the existing rule that says show the shape rather than narrating it, which governs how a session EXPLAINS something in conversation. This one governs what the BUILT SURFACE contains.

AUDIT SIGNAL: any structured surface shipped or reviewed without a visual is named out loud in that session's report as missing one, with what the visual should have shown. A review that passes a text-only board is itself the visible failure.

b587f6c2.gist: WHEN TO CONVENE A FRONTIER-MODEL COUNCIL — the decision procedure, so convening is never a mood or a ritual
b587f6c2.statement:
WHEN TO CONVENE A FRONTIER-MODEL COUNCIL — the decision procedure, so convening is never a mood or a ritual. A council meeting is a deliberative round table: two or more OUTSIDE frontier-model chairs (fresh context, no house anchoring) plus the host session, distinct lenses assigned per rule 81709f57, one identical brief to every chair.

CONVENE when ALL THREE hold:
1. NO DETERMINISTIC VERIFIER — the question cannot be settled by a test, a query, a gate, or a measured outcome. If a check can answer it, run the check instead.
2. WIDE OPTION SPACE OR AN ANCHORED HOST — more than two defensible shapes exist, or the host session helped build the premises under review (the anchoring is exactly why outside chairs earn their seat: they attack what the host treats as settled).
3. EXPENSIVE REVERSAL — the outcome hardens into schema, doctrine, security surface, or a partner's workflow, so changing it later costs a migration, a re-teach, or partner retraining.

DETECTABLE MOMENTS that make the test fire (so this does not decay into a judgment nobody makes mid-task): a system-domain design fork carrying the ❓ marker; any proposal for a new table, verb family, or mechanism class beyond a single obvious extension of an existing one; any change to which mechanism class governs a write surface; before ratifying any ORDER-class structural plan; when a partner asks an architecture "should we / which way" question with no checkable answer.

NEVER convene: for anything a test or query settles; for routine builds, copy, or deal work (the Deal Council and the writing gates own those lanes); as ritual on a question with no named fork — a panel without a fork is structure wearing the costume of rigor.

MECHANICS THAT MAKE IT WORTH THE TOKENS, each one evidence-backed from the first day's runs (2026-08-06): the HOST BRIEF IS LOAD-BEARING — it must carry the house constraints, because both outside chairs got the dossier question wrong until the connector-only-write-path constraint was supplied; the host STAKES ITS OWN POSITION before reading the chairs, so synthesis is a third view and not an echo; ROUND 2 runs only when round 1 produced genuine disagreement, and each chair then reads the others' positions for rebuttal and concession; the outcome LANDS VIA log-decision the same session, with the settled verdicts in the rationale, or the deliberation evaporates. Outside chairs ride existing subscriptions, so the marginal cost is host synthesis — acceptable for the triggered class and only for it.

RESEARCH-COUNCIL AMENDMENTS (2026-08-07, Joe's order to mine the published literature; load-bearing sources read raw per rule 94806da2 — arXiv 2605.29800 and 2510.07517): (1) ROUND 2 IS ANONYMIZED CROSS-REVIEW — when round 1 disagrees, chairs read each other's positions with model identities stripped, because identity-driven sycophancy is measured and widespread and anonymization forces judgment onto the argument. (2) UNANIMITY IS A SCRUTINY TRIGGER, NOT A CONFIDENCE SIGNAL — a measured panel of nine frontier judges carried only ~2 independent votes' worth of information because models miss the same items together; when all chairs agree, the host's synthesis must say what would have caught a shared blind spot (usually the re-run-the-evidence seat), never report agreement as proof. (3) A ROUND-2 REVERSAL IS ACCEPTED ONLY FOR NEW EVIDENCE — verbosity and confidence measurably flip judges without adding information, so a chair that changes position must name the fact that moved it or the reversal is noted and discounted. (4) SEAT DIVERSITY IS STRUCTURAL — never fill an additional seat with another instance of a family already seated wearing a different lens; correlated errors are why the panel exists, and a same-family seat reintroduces them. (5) THE PANEL STAYS SMALL — three to five seats captures most of the measurable ensemble benefit; growth past that is cost wearing the costume of rigor. The literature's core negative finding is recorded here so nobody relitigates it: multi-model debate frequently loses to one strong model plus a deterministic check, which is exactly why the three convene-conditions above remain the gate.

b7ec8f3b.statement: DOCTORCRE SURFACE GRAMMAR, from Joe's review of the V5-UX-S01 prototypes on 2026-09-16, applied site-wide: (1) A good title does the job; no descriptive sentence under a title, no "nothing needs you" / "one thing is broken, nothing is stuck" narration — that register is refused as AI voice. (2) Toggles (theme, density, motion) are single icons whose on/off state is shown by filled vs hollow color, not words; a dropdown shows its own title and then the selected option. (3) Tiles list their items directly; an item opens an on-screen popup with full detail and the ability to enter data or answer it, never a link that autoscrolls the same page; when a destination is a whole surface it opens in its own tab. (4) Times are AM/PM, never 24-hour; due dates use a real calendar picker with a typed-date fallback. (5) Doc is one floating icon at the bottom right on every tab, an actual LLM agent that reads the current page for context, with Quill dictation inside the chat window; no per-tile "Ask Doc" buttons. (6) Team is Joe and Dell by definition: never label "Joe and Dell" or "Team Book"; the combined deal list gets a plain name. (7) Kanban cards move by mouse drag with no Move button (a keyboard path stays available but not as a visible button). (8) Motion is slower and calmer, a slow disappearing ring rather than a fast spinner. (9) Every control that looks interactive must do something. (10) Repairs of known issues are reported as done, not queued for approval (see the companion rule on autonomous repair).

bbffc139.gist: THE LEDGER TRIGGERS. Joe's development kit has produced ZERO entries since it was enacted, and the cause is
bbffc139.statement:
THE LEDGER TRIGGERS. Joe's development kit (rules 21-23: override ledger, calibration ledger, compression reps, timing gym, close-before-open) has produced ZERO entries since it was enacted, and the cause is diagnosed: those rules say "when Joe makes a major call" or "when Joe states a significant prediction," which are judgments a session has to make about his speech mid-task, not detectable moments. That is the identical trap rule 74d6b19d already closed for taught rules by naming seven concrete triggers. The taught-rule half fires reliably and unprompted; the ledger half never fires. This rule extends the same mechanism to the ledgers. FIVE TRIGGERS, any one of which logs on the spot via log-decision, no permission asked: (1) JOE OVERRULES A RECOMMENDATION — he rejects an approach, corrects a framing, or picks the option the session argued against. Log the call, the session's position, his position, and later the outcome. Log it even when he turns out wrong; a ledger that only records his wins measures nothing. (2) HE STATES A PREDICTION OR A CONFIDENT CALL about how something will behave, what will work, or how long something will take. Capture his reasoning AT DECISION TIME, before the result is known, because a prediction logged after the fact is worthless for calibration. (3) HE COMPRESSES SOMETHING INTO A ONE-LINER THE SESSION THEN BUILDS ON — the test is not whether it sounds quotable, it is whether the session's next action changed because of it. Log as "Joe's framing" with the testable form. (4) HE RULES ON HOW SOMETHING IS STRUCTURED OR MODELLED in a way that settles a fork. (5) HE CORRECTS A FACT OR A PREMISE the session was operating on. BOUNDARY SWEEPS, mandatory, and they reuse the detectable moments that already work: before any commit, before any deploy, before writing a handoff or checkpoint, and whenever he changes subject, re-read the exchange since the last sweep and ask what of his belongs in a ledger and is not stored. THE VISIBILITY HALF, without which this decays like its predecessors: the ledgers get the same audit signal the compiled rules have. State the count in the session-start recitation alongside the rule counts, in the form "Rules loaded: N shared, M personal · ledger entries this month: X." Zero is a number Joe can see and challenge; silence is not. LOGGING IS FREE and needs no permission — a decision event binds nobody and costs nothing, so the bar to log is near-zero and the entries are never batched for later.

THE SCOPE, added 2026-08-09 on Joe's order "tighten the ledger triggers". EVERY TRIGGER ABOVE RUNS ONLY INSIDE THE WORK. This ledger is a development kit for calibrating his judgment on the business and the system; a turn about neither is out of scope no matter which words it contains. An exchange is in scope when EITHER his words carry a record ref or a CARR or system noun, OR the session's response to that turn touched the record layer, the repo or the vault — either alone, never both required, because a ruling can arrive in bare words while the session is deep in carr-system ("lets always rehearse on a branch first") and can equally arrive naming a client while the session does nothing but listen. Requiring both re-opens the misses this rule was written to close. AND A PAST-TENSE OUTCOME REPORT IS NOT A PREDICTION: trigger 2 is about how something WILL behave, captured at decision time, so "it worked" is the far end of that sentence and never trigger 2 on its own.

WHY THE SCOPE EXISTS, because the reason is the same disease as the original. On 2026-08-09 the hook fired twice inside a keyboard-repair thread with no CARR content at all: once on "i want it to be fully apple keyboard", once on "okay i think it worked". The honest answer on such a turn is "no entry", and answering no turn after turn is precisely how a gate becomes a rubber stamp. A ledger that cries wolf fails the same way the silent one did — it just fails while looking busy. THE FIX IS SCOPE, NOT SENSITIVITY: no trigger pattern was weakened, because each was added to close a real named miss and tightening them is how the zero-entry failure returns. The mechanism lives in hooks/ledger-sweep.py and its regression set, tools/test-ledger-scope.py, pins BOTH failure modes at once — every historical miss as a must-fire case, the two false positives as must-stay-silent — so a future tightening cannot quietly re-open the silence.
